verdicts.strongest_argument: The facts check out — I independently confirmed 61 of 80 open requisitions in Torrington and all nine of the cited third-shift titles exist on the careers site — but the INFERENCE is the consensus story, not new information, and two verifiable details break it. (1) The ramp itself is in the wire copy: on 2026-06-08 FuelCell publicly raised its Torrington capacity plan from 350 to 500 MW/yr at $200-275m capex, disclosed that a high-volume tape caster install had begun and a new conditioning room was commissioned, and reiterated the 100 MW-annualised EBITDA-breakeven target; CBIA (2026-06-11) and DCD carried it. Mass hiring at that plant is the mechanical footprint of an announced program, not a discovery. (2) The postings are not 'right now' — the Supervisor, Tape Casting (Third Shift) requisition has been live on LinkedIn for ~2 months (posted ~late June 2026) and shows a careers-site posted date of Aug 15, 2026, i.e. it is a REPOST of an unfilled req. A two-month-old, reposted third-shift supervisor opening is evidence the third shift is not running, which is the opposite of 'a line being commissioned.' (3) The shift designations do not support the inference the hunter draws from them: the 'Facility Tech (Third Shift)' posting states, verbatim, 'The hours for this position are M-F 3:30 pm to 11:30 pm' — identical to the site's own second-shift Process Operator schedule. At least one of the nine cited 'third shift' titles is a mislabelled second shift, and 'Supervisor, Tape Casting (Third Shift)' and 'Security Officer (3rd Shift)' state no clock hours at all. Janitor and Security Officer coverage is also consistent with a two-year construction site rather than a 24/7 production line. (4) Timing: the third-shift reqs I could date are Aug 4 and Aug 15, 2026, i.e. AFTER the quarter ended 2026-07-31, so they cannot show up in the printed quarter; and to the extent shift staffing does hit the P&L it is a near-term cost drag on a $35.6m-revenue quarter with negative product gross margin, so even the sign is contested. What I concede: no analyst note, wire story or company release has drawn out the shift build-out explicitly, the aggregator indexing (ZipRecruiter/Indeed/rejobs/LinkedIn) is genuinely obscure, and the put skew of +11.64 vol points says the market is not paying for a ramp surprise. That is why this is 55 and not 85.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Q2 FY26 release discloses the Torrington expansion to 'an annualized production rate of up to 500 MW' at $200-275m over 24 months, with the high-volume tape caster install begun and a new conditioning room commissioned as of 2026-05-31.
Trade press carries the $200-275m Torrington expansion to 500 MW annualised output, 'well above earlier expectations', framed around data-centre demand.

The flagship third-shift requisition (Supervisor, Tape Casting, Third Shift, Torrington) has been publicly posted on LinkedIn for ~2 months and shows as '2 months ago', so the third-shift build-out has been visible on aggregators since late June.
The posting titled 'Facility Tech (Third Shift)' states its hours as 'M-F 3:30 pm to 11:30 pm' — second-shift hours — showing the site's shift labels do not reliably denote an overnight shift.
Security Officer (3rd Shift) posted 2026-08-04 states no clock hours, only on-call flexibility; posted after the 2026-07-31 quarter end.

Management on the Q2 call: capacity plan raised from 350 to 500 MW/yr and 'once we achieve consistent production volumes at or above 100 megawatts on an annualized basis, we are targeting getting to adjusted EBITDA positive' — the ramp-to-volume story is stated guidance.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The ramp was announced into the 2026-06-08 print on which the stock fell 10.56%, and the stock is down a further 25.67% over 20 days while the third-shift reqs were live and aggregator-indexed. A +11.64 vol-point 25-delta put skew and 'downside paid' lean say the market is emphatically not pricing a capacity-ramp positive — which is the one thing that keeps this finding out of the 70s.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated, non-reposted set of third-shift reqs with genuine overnight clock hours (e.g. 11:30pm-7:30am) filled before 2026-07-31, or company confirmation on the call that a third production shift is actually running, would move this to 20-30.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The Form 4 is exactly as described — I verified reporting person Homer John Livingston III, Director, transaction date 2026-07-16, code P, 26,343 shares at a $18.7893 weighted average (range $18.71-$18.79), direct, 26,343 shares held after — so nothing here is factually wrong. It is also the single most mechanically-syndicated disclosure type in the market: GuruFocus published it on 2026-07-20, the day the Form 4 was filed, and TipRanks and Quiver Quantitative both ran it. Six weeks of public availability on every insider screen is the definition of in the price. On base rates, a single first-time director purchase of ~$495k — against ~78.3m shares outstanding post the July offering, i.e. about 0.03% of the company — has close to no predictive power for the next earnings reaction, and the tape says so directly: the stock has fallen from $18.79 to $16.72 since the buy, so the purchase is 11% underwater and the market has already overwhelmed it. Context makes it weaker still, not stronger: he bought nine days after the $225m offering priced at $21.00 on 2026-07-07, which is the textbook moment for a newly-seated director to demonstrate alignment below the deal price, and he bought two weeks before quarter-end, when a director seated on 2026-05-19 would have had little quarter-specific knowledge. I accept the fact and reject the size, not the sign.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Published the same day as the Form 4: Director Livingston III Homer John purchased 26,343 shares on 2026-07-16 at $18.79, ~$494,900, his first purchase.
Insider-tracking outlet headlines the identical purchase: 'Insider Purchase: Director at $FCEL Buys 26,343 Shares'.
TipRanks insider-trading news piece on the same FuelCell director purchase ('Insider Makes Bold Move on FuelCell Energy Shares').
The $225m offering priced at $21.00 (10,714,286 shares) with 78,322,459 shares outstanding after — the purchase came nine days later, below the offering price.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The stock has fallen ~11% below the purchase price since 2026-07-16 and 25.67% over 20 days, with puts bid at +11.64 vol points. If the market assigned information content to the buy, it is not visible anywhere in the tape or the skew.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A cluster — two or more officers or directors buying in size in August, especially inside the pre-print window and unpublished by the insider screens — would be a different finding and could justify 20-35.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every fact checks out against the 8-K: 12,000,000 warrant shares in three 4,000,000 tranches, $26.44 strike, first tranche vesting only on a non-refundable deposit equal to 16% of the order value for the 100 MW Phase 1, executed 2026-06-22. And I confirm the news drought — the investor-relations feed shows nothing after 'Siemens and FuelCell Energy Collaborate' on 2026-07-09 until the 2026-08-25 conference-call notice. But almost none of this is hidden. The strike is in a public 8-K and the spot is on the tape, so '58% above spot' is arithmetic anyone can do; the absence of news is the most visible fact about the name — a stock with no press release for seven weeks, down 25.67% in 20 days, carrying the most bid put skew of the day at +11.64 vol points and a 'downside paid' lean, is a market that has already marked the Fit Energy optionality down toward zero. Benzinga wrote precisely this thesis in August ('FuelCell Pullback Deepens as Investors Weigh Data Center Promise Against Near-Term Risks'). Two things also make the bear framing harsher than the documents support: the 2026-06-23 announcement states Fit made an immediate deposit for an initial 30 MW with deliveries beginning later this year, so Phase 0 is firm and not silence; and the unvested warrants only cancel 24 months after issuance, so ten weeks without a Phase 1 election is well inside the contractual clock. The 'within this fiscal year' quote is real and I verified it on the Q2 call, but FY ends 2026-10-31 — two months after this print — so a missed conversion cannot be scored at this print, only worried about, and worrying about it is what the skew is already paying for. Finally, an absence is genuinely unfalsifiable in the way the brief warns: I can confirm no 8-K exists, but I cannot distinguish 'no deal' from 'deal not yet announceable', and the market cannot either, which is exactly why it is already in the discount rather than being a discovery.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Discloses the Fit Energy USA CEPA with 12,000,000 warrant shares in three 4,000,000 tranches at a $26.44 strike, tranche 1 vesting on a non-refundable deposit of 16% of the 100 MW Phase 1 order value, unvested warrants cancelling 24 months after issuance.
Public announcement of the up-to-380 MW agreement, with an immediate deposit for an initial 30 MW beginning delivery later in 2026 and Phases 1-3 at Fit's sole election.

August wire piece explicitly framing the selloff as the data-centre promise weighed against near-term risks including dilution from the $225m July offering, 5% revenue decline and backlog down 9.9% to $1.14bn.
Confirms management's own words, 'with the goal of converting submitted proposals into contracted backlog within this fiscal year' — the commitment is published, not hunted.

Prospectus risk language flags 'the risk that our bid awards will not convert to contracts or that our contracts will not convert to revenue' — the conversion risk is a disclosed risk factor marketed to buyers of the July offering.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: -25.67% over 20 days and -53.56% from the 52-week high on no company news since 2026-07-09; 25-delta put skew +11.64 vol points, the most negative of the day, put/call OI 1.03, event-implied move 10.36%. This is the shape of a market that has already removed the Fit Energy upside from the price and is paying for more downside.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that consensus still carries a Phase 1 100 MW order in FY26 revenue or backlog — e.g. a published sell-side model with the deposit booked in Q4 — would restore real surprise capacity and move this to 35-45.

interactions: FCEL#0 and FCEL#2 are near-mirrors of one question, and they partly cannibalise each other: #0 reads the Torrington 24/7 staffing as evidence demand is landing, while #2 reads the ten-week silence as evidence it is not. Both cannot be independent edges — capacity being built ahead of contracted orders is itself the bear case (cash burn against a $200-275m capex program funded by a $225m July equity raise), so #0's own fact strengthens #2's conclusion rather than offsetting it. They also rest on the same document: the 2026-06-08 Q2 package supplies both the 500 MW / tape-caster ramp that #0 is inferring and the verbatim 'converting submitted proposals into contracted backlog within this fiscal year' commitment that #2 measures against. Separately, FCEL#1 and FCEL#2 share the July 2026 offering as unstated context — the $21.00 pricing on 2026-07-07 is both why Livingston's $18.79 buy looks like alignment optics and part of why the stock de-rated; and note the share count relevant to sizing any of these is 78.3m post-offering, not the 63.5m on the 2026-04-30 balance sheet.
